title: checksum-mismatch-debug-playbook
content:
Context:
- Incident: model load failures during private deployment staging (VPC). Multiple runs fail when loading sharded checkpoint. Symptoms: loader throws checksum/EOF errors or torch serialization errors intermittently across nodes.
- Model: alexa-style decoder-only 7.5B, saved with HF-compatible sharded state dict (weights-00000-of-00008.bin + model-index.json).
- Storage: S3 (third-party), fetched to local host via s3fs/fuse for launcher. Also reproduces when downloading via aws s3 cp to local disk.

Initial error snippets observed (collected from node logs):
- "RuntimeError: unexpected EOF, expected to read 32768 bytes but got 0"
- "ValueError: Checksum verification failed for weights-00003.bin (expected f1d3ff84, got 3b6e20c8)"
- "torch.serialization.pickle.UnpicklingError: invalid load key, '\u0000'"
- "Failed to mmap file: Invalid argument"

Commands I ran while reproducing and collecting artifacts (timestamps omitted):
- ls -lh weights-* | sort -n
- sha256sum weights-* > /tmp/sha256_local.txt
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/chat7b/sharded/weights-00003.bin . --no-progress
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/chat7b/sharded/weights-00003.bin /tmp/remote-downloaded.bin
- cmp --silent weights-00003.bin /tmp/remote-downloaded.bin || echo "DIFFER"
- python -c "import torch; torch.load('weights-00003.bin')"  # raises EOF/UnpicklingError on failing files
- head -c 64 weights-00003.bin | hexdump -C
- file weights-00003.bin  # check for compression/header
- stat -c '%s %n' weights-* > /tmp/sizes_local.txt
- aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key chat7b/sharded/weights-00003.bin --query '{Size:ContentLength, ETag:ETag}'
- md5sum weights-* > /tmp/md5_local.txt
- curl -I https://s3-us-west.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/chat7b/sharded/weights-00003.bin

What I observed:
- Size mismatch: occasionally the local file size is smaller than the S3 head-object ContentLength. This correlates with EOF errors.
- Checksum mismatch: md5/sha256 between local copy and the manifest (we keep a manifest of sha256s) differs for a small subset (~1-3%) of shards in heavy parallel downloads.
- When I re-downloaded the same shard (aws s3 cp again) the new copy sometimes matches expected checksum. Suggests transient transfer corruption or partial reads when using parallel fetchers.
- Filesystems: failures more frequent when using s3fs fuse mounts and when parallel workers download into the same directory. Using aws cli to download directly to local disk reduced but did not eliminate failures under load.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Partial/Truncated Downloads due to network timeouts or termination in multipart objects leading to 0-byte tail truncation. Evidence: smaller file sizes + EOF errors.
2) Corrupted multipart upload on S3 side (bad ETag/part mismatch). But fewer signs because re-downloads can succeed and S3 head-object shows posted size.
3) s3fs/fuse caching/incomplete flush causing readers to see a half-written file when another process writes concurrently. Evidence: higher incidence when s3fs used.
4) Tooling issue: our manifest generation step might record checksums from a different version of the file (e.g., gzip vs raw) causing perceived mismatch.
5) Disk-level issues on staging VMs (rare) or antivirus interfering (unlikely on Linux infra).

Quick diagnostic checklist to run during next failure (short actionable steps for on-call):
- Immediately run: stat -c '%s' weights-0000?.bin and compare to S3 head-object ContentLength for each shard.
- Compute sha256sum and md5sum locally and compare with model-index.json manifest values.
- If mismatch, re-run aws s3 cp <object> to /tmp/<object>.retry and cmp files. If retry matches manifest, suspect transient network.
- Check for concurrent writers: lsof | grep weights-00003.bin and ps aux | grep model-fetcher to see race conditions.
- If using s3fs, remount with direct_io and no_readahead to reduce caching artifacts. Command tried: fusermount -u /mnt/s3 && s3fs redwood-models /mnt/s3 -o use_cache=/tmp/s3cache -o direct_io -o allow_other
- Check kernel dmesg for I/O errors: dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep -i 'I/O error|md0|s3fs|fuse'

Workarounds that reduced incidence during testing:
- Serializing shard downloads (worker picks a shard and downloads to a tmp file then atomically mv into place) eliminated race-related partial reads. Pseudocode: curl -o /tmp/weights-00003.bin.$$ <s3-url> && mv /tmp/weights-00003.bin.$$ weights-00003.bin
- Adding simple retry logic with exponential backoff for aws s3 cp reduced failures dramatically. Implemented in launcher: up to 5 retries on non-200 HTTP codes and on checksum mismatch.
- Avoid s3fs for hot-path: prefer direct aws s3 cp or pre-stage artifacts to ephemeral instance store.

Longer-term fixes / engineering follow-ups (tickets to open):
- Add atomic-write pattern to the model fetcher so files are not visible until complete. (Ticket: MODELINFRA-4521)
- Add a verification step in the loader that checks shard checksums before any torch.load attempts; fail fast with clear message and a deterministic retry. (Ticket: MODELINFRA-4522)
- Add monitoring: percent of shards failing checksum per deploy, and histograms of retry counts. (Ticket: OBS-1317)
- Investigate S3 multipart upload toolchain (who/what wrote these checkpoints). If uploads were produced by an older client, verify ETag/part handling. (Ticket: STORAGE-889)
- Document best practices for downstream (private) deployments: avoid fuse mounts for model artifacts, use direct downloads, enforce tmp-file -> rename atomic staging. (Docs PR: internal/docs#models-s3-fetching)

Notes for reproducer and data collection (for engineers who will pick this up):
- Repro steps I used: spin up a 8-worker launcher in staging, start parallel downloads via s3fs mount and trigger model start. Watch for 1-2 failures per 100 deployments.
- Attach full set of sha256_local.txt, md5_local.txt, sizes_local.txt and s3 head-object outputs in the bug report.
- Collected example bad file and good file with hexdump of first 128 bytes for forensic comparison. Store artifacts in s3://redwood-debug/casey/checksum-playbook/<timestamp>/

Edge cases & oddities seen:
- One shard had correct size but differing checksum — hexdump showed a repeating 0x00 suffix of a few KB. Suggests zero-padding after truncated write or partial overwrite with zeros by some process.
- Another node showed mmap failure; mounting with -o direct_io resolved it briefly -> points back to fuse caching behavior.

Action items (assigned):
- Casey: raise MODELINFRA-4521/4522 and OBS-1317, attach artifacts. (done draft)
- Dana Lopez: validate upload pipeline and identify uploader client version. (assigned STORAGE-889)
- SRE on-call: add alert for >0.5% shard checksum failures in a 1h window.

Open questions (for post-mortem):
- Are corrupted uploads happening during checkpoint creation? Or only during download/transfer?
- Can we change CI to verify artifacts after every upload (post-checkpoint)?
- Should we replace s3fs-based deployments entirely for private clusters, or provide a hardened mount command?

Notes to self (todo):
- Add unit test in model-fetcher that simulates partial file (truncate) and ensures loader does not attempt partial torch.load.
- Add better error text for operators: include expected size/checksum in the log line and the s3 key.
